sections.value:
ROUND 1 performance verdict: PASS-WITH-NOTES.
Subject: pr:317
Head: 4771b4b3d7ac93dd836be90cc3ca5d5d2dd5fb36

The instrumentation adds bounded in-process work, no SQL, event write, log, task spawn, poll, timer or process-launch site. No demonstrated resource-cost breach blocks this head. The source supports measuring stage wall time, including awaited pool/worker/scheduler delays; it does not isolate pool wait from those other costs or directly measure CPU.

Own overhead, verified from identity.rs:1237-1310,1475-1492,1575-1578 and route_counts.rs:350-480:
- A successful pane whoami starts 5 + L StageSpans: seat-list, Codex, role, FYI, encode, and one per liveness-helper invocation L. Each span reads the clock at start and elapsed at drop. With L=1 and about 10 calls/s this is about 120 clock reads/s, not a new polling loop.
- One task-local scope holds an eight-u64 StageTimes value (64 bytes). Span/row updates copy that value in the request's task; they do not allocate, lock, or update shared counters per liveness iteration. Scope access also rides request-future polling.
- Completion adds three counters unconditionally (calls, list_rows, liveness_reads), plus at most six nonzero stage totals: 3-9 relaxed atomic adds/call. GET and POST also add an Arc clone/drop pair, approximately two additional reference-count RMWs. At 10 calls/s that is approximately 50-110 added shared atomic operations/s, excluding existing outer route counters.
- Counter storage is fixed: nine AtomicU64s per RouteCounts, not per seat or caller. Ping reads those nine values and builds a fixed six-key stage map; this allocation is on snapshot, not on every whoami.
- Other routes using resolve_seat still pay its clock pairs and task-local try_with attempts, although they record no whoami data. Price that by resolver invocation rate and L, not only the roughly 10 whoamis/s.

Diagnostic notes, non-blocking:
1. Add the Arc pair to the cost accounting, and preserve the distinction between "records nothing outside whoami" and "costs nothing outside whoami." Neither needs a different architecture.
2. Stages are elapsed wall time, not CPU or exclusive pool-acquisition time. They include awaits within each guarded operation; six buckets do not distinguish pool wait, SQLite work, worker-thread hops and scheduler delay. Residual outer route time also contains instrumentation, unguarded refusal awaits, auth/extraction and per-span microsecond truncation. Sub-microsecond stages can legitimately sum to zero.
3. Match cohorts: whoami.calls combines GET and POST handlers that actually entered the scope, while route counts also include pre-handler refusals. Snapshots are independently relaxed reads, not one transaction. Use matched delta windows, both method routes where applicable, and avoid interpreting a transient negative residual as a behavior failure.

Evidence:
- just pr-freeze 317: FINAL at the full head, CLEAN, all five latest checks passed; branch schema48 predates main49, no migration added.
- Exact-head CI44894876595, successful Rust job136818279375, upload artifact14704165009: 2,790 tests passed overall, six skipped. Independently read JUnit: 21 relevant route-count/identity/whoami/FYI cases and spawn-site sensors passed, including whoami_stages_count_only_inside_a_whoami and all six spawn-site checks.
- A source diff confirms only timing wrappers/notes, fixed counters/snapshot fields, one test and docs were added. Whoami's underlying store/transport work is unchanged. This performance verdict does not substitute for the separate correctness/security reviews.
- No local instrument-only latency benchmark was run. Operation counts above are source proof; the producer's removed offline store benchmark is not a reproducible overhead receipt.
- Live BEFORE only, daemon35dd41ac91/PID72066, UTC2026-11-21T10:52:34.760819Z to10:52:54.784821Z, monotonic20.023932s: POST whoami182 completions,9.0891/s,444.43us active-wall/call; spawns delta0. CPU time+1.67s (8.34% of one core), RSS99,648->101,520KiB. Other fleet activity and review checks existed; none of this is PR317 attribution or AFTER improvement. The lower current wall time is a different cohort from the older ~2.4ms figure.
- Separate subsequent just spawn-rate --seconds 20: machine205.5 launches/s,183.7/s sampled, no daemon descendants sampled. This busy observer did not overlap the preceding process/route window; machine rates are not attributed to this PR.
- harness boot ready=false (missing local vitest). harness checks --quick exit1: eight dependency/ambient-tool failures; native and SDK stages passed; heavy Rust/route/smoke skipped. C25: no install or symlink, no claimed green local full gate.
- No bounce, deployment, pane input, second daemon, source edit, local Rust build or boundary mutant rerun. Review worktree remains clean. Both performance/317 and performance/314 holdings remain until merge.

Harness lesson: keep a reusable instrument-on/off overhead receipt and matched route/stage/process windows. A bounded source-work count is valuable, but is not measured microseconds of added overhead or proof that a SQL safeguard should be removed.
